stimulus.source_note: Photograph: Reverend Jerry Falwell at an 'I Love America' rally, Ohio Statehouse, Columbus, Ohio, September 17, 1979, by David E. Lucas (Columbus Metropolitan Library, via DPLA/Wikimedia Commons), public domain. Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.14; 5 Steps Ch. 28; Princeton Ch. 12).
stimulus.text: The photograph shows the Reverend Jerry Falwell speaking into a microphone on the steps of the Ohio Statehouse in Columbus, Ohio, on September 17, 1979, at an 'I Love America' rally. Behind him stands a choir of young men in white suits and young women in long red dresses with their heads bowed, and six American flags stand before the building's stone columns.

stem: Background: Falwell founded the Moral Majority in 1979. What did the Moral Majority do?

options.text: It banned every church in America from taking part in politics.
options.misconception: The Moral Majority brought churches into politics, the opposite of banning them.

options.text: It organized evangelical Christians to vote against abortion and liberal social change.
It supported the Equal Rights Amendment and campaigned for its passage.
options.misconception: The Moral Majority opposed the Equal Rights Amendment, along with abortion and gay rights.

options.text: It worked to keep Christians out of elections and voting booths.
options.misconception: The Moral Majority registered voters and backed candidates, so it pushed Christians into elections.

rationales.A: Background: The Moral Majority brought churches into politics, the opposite of banning them.
rationales.B: Background: Falwell founded the Moral Majority in 1979 to register evangelical voters and fight abortion, the Equal Rights Amendment, and other liberal changes.
rationales.C: Background: The Moral Majority opposed the Equal Rights Amendment, along with abortion and gay rights.
rationales.D: Background: The Moral Majority registered voters and backed candidates, so it pushed Christians into elections.
rationales.general:
1. The photograph shows Falwell preaching politics on capitol steps in 1979, the year he founded the Moral Majority.
2. Background: The group registered evangelical voters and campaigned against abortion and the Equal Rights Amendment.
3. Its work was to bring Christians into elections, not to keep them out.
Remember: A group's name tells its aim, so ask what its members actually did.
